title: Air India Wins FlightGlobal Digital Leadership Award for Tech Transformation
excerpt: The Tata-owned carrier takes the Digital Leadership prize at the 2026 Airline Strategy Awards in London, capping a $200 million technology overhaul that rebuilt its systems from scratch.
body:
• Air India won the Digital Leadership award at the 2026 Airline Strategy Awards, organized by FlightGlobal’s Airline Business in London on July 19
  • The airline invested $200 million to rebuild its entire technology infrastructure, migrating legacy systems to the cloud under Tata Group ownership
  • Air India’s mobile app now has 28 million downloads and a 4.8-star rating, with the industry’s first generative AI virtual assistant, AI.g
  • The digital overhaul is part of the Vihaan.AI transformation that has expanded Air India’s fleet from 70 to 300 aircraft

Recognition on the Global Stage

Air India has been awarded the Digital Leadership prize at the 2026 Airline Strategy Awards, held in London on July 19 ahead of the Farnborough Airshow. The awards, organized by FlightGlobal’s Airline Business magazine and Korn Ferry, recognize strategic excellence across nine categories in the global aviation industry.

The recognition caps a sweeping technology transformation under Tata Group ownership that has reshaped nearly every digital touchpoint of India’s flag carrier. Led by Dr. Satya Ramaswamy, Air India’s Chief Digital and Technology Officer, the airline invested $200 million to overhaul an infrastructure so outdated that its SAP mainframe — housed in a neglected building near Delhi Airport — was, by Ramaswamy’s account, literally falling apart.

Rebuilding From the Ground Up

When the Tata Group reacquired Air India in 2022, the airline’s technology stack was minimal, limited largely to systems required for regulatory compliance. A modern airline typically operates 140 to 150 systems. Air India had to build most of them from scratch.

“Transformation is about people, process and technology — but above all, it’s about purpose. We believe in the future of India. And India had a rightful place in aviation once. Now, we need to give it back.”

— Dr. Satya Ramaswamy, Chief Digital and Technology Officer, Air India

The rebuild encompassed six core customer-facing digital channels: the mobile app, website, notification systems, the AI.g chatbot, third-party APIs, and the in-flight entertainment system. Behind these, enterprise systems for finance, HR, crew management, and engineering platforms were replaced entirely.

The most consequential technical decision was migrating the legacy SAP mainframe to the cloud — a high-risk move that defied industry convention but succeeded through what partners described as precise execution. The migration enabled the complex integration of Air India and Vistara, which required transferring 212 aircraft, 90 airports, and 9.2 million loyalty program members in under a year.

Measurable Results

The digital transformation has produced concrete outcomes. Air India’s redesigned mobile app carries a 4.8-star rating on both iOS and Android, ranking among the highest-rated airline apps globally, with approximately 28 million downloads. The website now sees 11 million visits per month — nearly four times higher than two years ago — and supports roughly 6.5 million direct ticket bookings monthly.

The airline’s generative AI virtual assistant, AI.g, has handled over 8 million queries since its May 2023 launch, averaging 30,000 daily interactions with a 97 percent containment rate — resolving most inquiries autonomously while escalating only 3 percent to human agents. Ramaswamy has noted that the cost of a query through AI.g is one-hundredth the cost of a call center interaction.

The digital overhaul has also earned prior recognition, including the Red Dot Award for design, the Stevie Award for app innovation, and the 2025 Adobe Experience Maker of the Year — a first for any Indian airline.

Significance for the Diaspora

For NRI travelers, the technology transformation translates directly into a more reliable booking, check-in, and travel experience. Real-time flight status updates, streamlined digital check-in, and the AI.g assistant — which handles queries across multiple channels — address friction points that diaspora travelers have historically encountered with Air India.

The award arrives as Air India continues its Vihaan.AI transformation program, which has expanded its fleet from 70 to 300 aircraft and increased its market share from single digits to 30 percent. The carrier has placed orders for 570 new aircraft and is rolling out cabin retrofits across its existing fleet, positioning it to compete credibly with the Gulf and East Asian carriers that NRI travelers have increasingly favored.
